newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish C.Bank governor says no decision on EMU rate.
newsitem.headline: Irish C.Bank governor says no decision on EMU rate.

text.p: Central Bank of Ireland governor Maurice O'Connell said on Tuesday that the European Union had not yet made a decision on the exchange rates at which countries would join EMU and there were "a number of possibilities" for the rate at which Ireland would join.
"Nothing at all has been decided. It is much too early to settle this," he told a news conference to launch the bank's annual report.
"There are a number of possibilities being mentioned, " the governor said.
O'Connell was responding to questions about speculation that the Irish pound may have to fall substantially against the mark in the ERM to reach the rate at which it will join EMU.
Market speculation along these lines caused fierce selling of the Irish currency in April and in May and led to heavy central bank intervention to defend the currency.
